fields.AN_Notes: Narrative review of AI in social sciences and social work 2022-2025. Its section 'Algorithmic Discrimination and Bias' structures the synthesis around low-income and minority families flagged in child welfare and welfare (Socioeconomic) and COMPAS (Race_Ethnicity); disabled individuals and single mothers appear once in a cited French case and are not coded. Harm: flagging through biases in historical training data in allocation decisions, coded as Indirect_Discrimination since the review names a data proxy, not the group attribute, as mechanism. Mitigation from the synthesis: diverse training data (Pre_Processing), adversarial debiasing and fairness constraints (In_Training), bias audits and human oversight (Organisational_Process); the review reports implementation in pilot programs without results, hence Demonstrated as a synthesised status. Integrity note: several references carry placeholder URLs (https://www.ap.org/xxxx) and shifted years or DOIs for well-known works (Angwin 2023, Buolamwini and Gebru 2022), so the reference basis needs expert checking.

fields.AN_Notes: Survey and taxonomy of intersectional fairness notions and mitigation in ML. Gender and race are the worked axes (Figure 1, Black women example); disability, religion, socioeconomic status appear in single cited works or dataset tables. Harm types structuring the synthesis: accuracy and worst-case performance gaps of intersectional subgroups (Disparate_Performance) and outcome-ratio notions derived from the 80 percent disparate-impact rule (Indirect_Discrimination by the YMABYPKF anchor); the survey itself does not classify direct versus indirect discrimination. Mitigation stages from the taxonomy: dataset coverage for intersectional groups (Pre_Processing), in-processing DRO, adversarial reweighting and auditing games (In_Training), multicalibration boosting and prediction flipping (Post_Processing). Evaluated is a synthesised status from reported experimental results of cited methods, not an own experiment. Gender is handled as a categorical attribute ('male/female for a binary gender'). Feministisch ja rests on Crenshaw's intersectionality as the core concept; Gender teilweise because gender is one component axis of an intersectional fairness survey.
